He is the author of ten books, including the autobiographical "Maggie’s American Dream: The Life and Times of a Black Family", 1988; "Leave No Child Behind: Preparing Today's Youth for Tomorrow's World", 2004; and his most recent book, "What I Learned in School: Reflections on Race, Child Development, and School Reform", 2009.  He has also written more than 150 articles for Parents (magazine) and more than 300 articles on children's health and development and race relations.  Dr. Comer has also served as a consultant to the Children's Television Workshop (Sesame Workshop) which produces Sesame Street and The Electric Company (1971 TV series).  He is a co-founder and past president of the Black Psychiatrists of America and has served on the board of several universities, foundations, and corporations.  He has also lectured and consulted widely not only across the United States at different universities, medical schools, and scientific associations, but also around the world in places such as London, Paris, Tokyo, Dakar, Senegal and Sydney, Australia.  For his work and scholarship, Dr. Comer has been awarded 47 honorary degrees and has been recognized by numerous organizations.
